elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Retained 15.2(a)(i): "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement or its rights and obligations hereunder in whole or in part to any Affiliate of Sanofi" — untouched by the redline, so the Customer-side affiliate carve-out survives verbatim.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Rewritten 15.2(a)(ii) preserves the Sanofi limb in substance: "Sanofi may, without consent of RevMed, assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest or assignee or purchaser ... in connection with the sale of all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction." All three triggers (merger, acquisition, substantially-all-assets sale) are expressly present.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: After the edit no RevMed assignment route is consent-free: the chapeau bars assignment "without the consent of the other Party, except as follows"; (a)(i) permits RevMed affiliate assignment only "with the consent of Sanofi"; and (a)(ii) now permits the Change-of-Control successor assignment "only with the prior written consent of Sanofi." The former "Either Party may, without consent of the other Party" no-consent route for RevMed has been removed.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Both RevMed-side permissions carry the standard: (a)(i) "(not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned)" (retained) and new (a)(ii) "(not to be unreasonably withheld)". The chapeau's residual consent for wholly unpermitted assignments is silent on the standard, which is Customer-favourable and not a defect.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: New (a)(ii) inserts "and in no event to a competitor of Sanofi" on the only RevMed successor/Change-of-Control route; every other RevMed route (affiliate under (a)(i), anything else under the chapeau) is consent-gated, so no drafting path lets RevMed reach a Sanofi competitor over Sanofi's objection. Note as a residual point only: the express competitor bar is textually confined to (a)(ii), so a RevMed-Affiliate assignment under (a)(i) is policed solely by the reasonableness-qualified consent.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The only Change-of-Control termination mechanic in the cited language runs the other way: 12.2(a)(ii) "For a Change of Control of RevMed ... Sanofi will have the option to either (A) terminate this Agreement in its entirety". Nothing in the rendered text gives RevMed a termination or re-pricing right on a Sanofi Change of Control, and the redline adds none.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: After the edit the successor right is asymmetric: Sanofi may assign to a successor "without consent of RevMed", while RevMed "may, only with the prior written consent of Sanofi ... assign this Agreement in whole to its successor in interest". There is no mutual no-consent successor right, so the fallback's first element fails (deliberately, since the drafter targeted preferred).

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: Neither limb of (a)(ii) imposes a written-notice obligation on a successor assignment; Sanofi's limb is silent and RevMed's is consent-based rather than notice-based. (12.2(a)(ii)'s notice duty is a termination-option trigger for a RevMed Change of Control, not an assignment notice.)

A no-consent non-successor exception is retained: (a)(i) lets "Sanofi ... without consent of RevMed, assign ... to any Affiliate of Sanofi". Under the ASSIGN fallback rule any retained no-consent non-successor exception defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The chapeau consent requirement for assignments outside (a)(i)-(ii) carries no reasonableness qualifier; the "not to be unreasonably withheld" language appears only in the two enumerated exceptions, so the general "other assignments" consent is unqualified.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: the two Customer-side carve-outs are retained verbatim, RevMed's former no-consent Change-of-Control assignment is converted to a Sanofi-consent right with a reasonableness standard, an express "in no event to a competitor of Sanofi" bar is added, and no RevMed termination right attaches to a Sanofi Change of Control.

Fallback is not met (no mutual no-consent successor right, no written-notice mechanic, retained Sanofi-affiliate no-consent exception, unqualified chapeau consent) — this is acceptable because the checklists are alternative and the preferred level is complete; targeting fallback here would also have surrendered the retained Sanofi affiliate carve-out.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only 15.2(a)(ii), the restructuring of the shared "Either Party may, without consent" opener is necessary because the two limbs now diverge, Sanofi's limb is reproduced with its full scope ("all or substantially all of its assets to which this Agreement relates, or in connection with a merger, acquisition or similar transaction"), and nothing outside the checklist (no notice tail, no survival or expense language, no re-pricing or firewall additions) is inserted.

Intent is preserved: 12.2(a)(ii)'s Sanofi termination option on a RevMed Change of Control, the 15.2 Acquiror-IP firewall conditions, and 15.3(c)(ii)C's post-termination royalty tail all continue to operate; a consented RevMed Change-of-Control assignment still occurs, so no cross-reference is left dangling and no retained sentence contradicts the edit.

Optional hardening (not a completeness defect): if you want the competitor bar to be unconditional across every route, move "and in no event to a competitor of Sanofi" into the 15.2(a) chapeau rather than leaving it inside the (a)(ii) successor limb, since (a)(i) affiliate assignments are currently policed only by reasonableness-qualified consent.
Margin comment accurately describes the two operative changes and cites the playbook position without over-claiming; no promise in the comment is doing work the operative text does not do.
